also: pass the papers to the front

terms.gloss: bring before, hand in (to an authority)
terms.grammar: verb, irregular, transitive; ad + acc. of the authority
evidence: Cic. Fam. 5.20.3: ratiōnēs dēferre, to hand in one’s accounts (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To bring something down to the place where it is dealt with: accounts or names to the treasury (ad aerārium), a matter to the senate or to a judge. So it fits a formal submission. It also means to report or denounce (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, transitive; the person in the dative
terms.comment: The everyday word for handing in homework or a form (see give).
evidence: Traupman 25: Trāde mihi., hand it in

phrases.english: Hand your homework in to the teacher tomorrow.
Pass the papers to the front.

sources: Lewis & Short: defero · Lewis & Short: trado
